corrected_content.problem:
Consider the matrix 
$D=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 3 & 6 & 15 \\ 5 & 11 & 28\end{bmatrix}.$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(D).$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(D),$ we reduce the matrix $D$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 3 & 6 & 15 \\ 5 & 11 & 28\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 11 & 28\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 5 & 11 & 28 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${d}_{1}$ and ${d}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(D)$ is $\{{d}_{1},{d}_{2}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\left\{\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6 \\ 11\end{bmatrix}\right\}.
$$
